_comment: The merchant and the chest. Card rewards are NOT listed here — they are drawn from content/cards.json by rarity, the way Slay the Spire rolls each of the three offers independently, so a fixed offer list can never drift from the card pool. What lives here is priced inventory and the removal ladder. Currency is focus, earned mainly by refusing rewards: sts-fidelity.md calls escalating removal cost the mechanism that gives the deck cap teeth, so it is emulated exactly.

removal._comment: 75 gold rising 25 every time removal is used anywhere in the run, scaled to our focus economy. Free removal makes bloat costless and the lean-deck tension collapses.

reward_rates._comment: Rarity roll per offer, with the rare-drought offset from the original: the offset starts negative, climbs each time a common is rolled, and resets when a rare appears. This is why the first reward of an act is effectively never rare.

campfire._comment: With no HP there is nothing to heal, so Rest and Smith become Smith and Prune. Both still spend the same non-renewable floor, which is the tension that actually mattered. Slay the Spire 2 grew rest sites to nine options (Rest, Smith, Dig, Lift, Cook, Clone, Hatch, Mend, Kindle); we keep two plus a relic-gated third, because options with no cost are not choices. `draws` says what an option pulls and from where, so the blurb's promise is data the engine honours rather than prose it can contradict — the shared `treasure` table is 43% potions by weight, so Dig has to filter it to keep its word.

options.name: Prune
options.blurb: Remove one card from the deck.

options.name: Dig
options.blurb: Draw one relic from the chest pool.
